row.models_note: Sonnet only by design (rule 12: completes sv-b1's Sonnet arm); Haiku's arm complete and failed; Opus would need about 270 more items, about $3.80, past the cap left.
row.odds_reason: Committed dry run puts P(pass) near 0.10 (0.013 to 0.38); literature row 0.12, under-$1 row 0.18, model referee 0.19, said-vs-did 0 of 2; layer 2's 0.50 rests on four bets.

row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is power: about 16 back-downs in 300 items leave the margin's interval about 0.3 wide, so even a real lead over question length reads as fail.
row.prior_work: **Mixed; no paper relates a separately stated number to backing down.** Huang 2026, SycoLens (arXiv 2610.06522; opus-5, sonnet-5, sonnet-4.6, haiku-4.5 and seven other models): answer changes concentrate on items near the model's own sampling boundary (+39.7 points pooled), yet for the most-moved models about half the effect comes from items never wavered on, and a bare "Are you sure?" moved cross-model means only 1.8–2.9 points. Li, Krishnan & Padman 2026 (arXiv 2602.13093; nine models incl. a Claude 4.5): log-probability confidence gave flip rates of 9.3%, 6.7% and 6.2% from low to high tercile, a shallow gradient (predicts fail at a 0.10 margin). Saadat & Nemzer 2026 (arXiv 2603.03330): Claude Sonnet 4.5 abandoned 6.9% of correct answers under "Are you sure?". In people, low own confidence predicts adopting another's view (Moussaïd et al. 2013, PLoS ONE). Sources: `map/reads/remap-2026-11-05-sv-b1.md`. **What this bet adds:** a separately stated 0–100 number, item by item, on Claude Sonnet 5.5, against simple guesses that include question type and length, with a within-type test (P16). The odds sit at the low end because the closest numbers in print (Li et al.) predict a shallow gradient.

row.title: Within obscure trivia alone, does the stated number predict declining under a penalty?
row.models_note: Haiku and Sonnet 300 items, Opus 100 (rule 12: thinking cannot be turned off).
row.odds_reason: The dry run gives 0.81 if wave-1 replicates but only 0.10 to 0.48 under the logistic worlds. The weak said-vs-did (0/2) and literature (0.12) rows offset layer 2 (0.50, n=4).
row.human_odds_note: Sean's card event is the map's draft rule (three guesses, no within-topic condition); reported as secondary (9).
row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that Haiku's ratings are so tied (most at 95–97) that its number cannot lead topic or answer type by 0.10, leaving only Sonnet passing.
row.prior_work: **Predicts a hit in direction; the margin is not in print.** Kumaran 2026 (arXiv 2606.29490, single author; within SimpleQA, verbal confidence elicited in a separate call, no stated penalty): verbal confidence separated abstaining from committing at AUROC 0.79/0.78 (Gemma 3 27B, class/numeric), 0.80/0.60 (Gemma 4 31B), 0.71/0.84 (GPT-4o) and 0.65/0.88 (Qwen3 235B), and an item-difficulty control removed under 2 points in all SimpleQA cells but one; no length, topic or answer-type baseline; no Claude. Koriat & Goldsmith 1996 (Psychological Review 103:490; people, one item set, a stated penalty): confidence-volunteering gamma .97 (recall). Wagner 2026 (arXiv 2607.08456; small open models) warns that a bag-of-words guess on the question reached 0.87 for answerability, so a surface guess can be strong. Jozefowiez, Staddon & Cerutti 2009 (CCBR 4:29) predict that an observable item property can carry "uncertain" responses, which is why this bet holds the trivia bit constant and adds topic and answer type as rivals. **What this bet adds:** three Claude 5.5 models, an announced penalty, and a margin over simple guesses that include SimpleQA's own topic and answer type, with a within-topic test (P16). The odds are stated with Kumaran's range in view: it predicts the direction, not a 0.10 lead over item properties.

fields.novelty_line: **Novelty:** partly new. Pawitan & Holmes (2025, Harvard Data Science Review 7.1; arXiv 2412.15296) already report the direction on GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo and Mistral Large 2: a 0–100 confidence score asked in a separate session went with keeping the answer after "Please think again carefully" (GPT-4o kept 0.77 of answers scored below 95 against 0.93 at 95 or above, P = 0.0065; P from 0.0065 to 0.093 across the three models). Kumaran et al. (2025, arXiv 2507.03120) find that change of mind under opposing advice falls with log-probability initial confidence (Gemma 3, R² = 0.96), while Li, Krishnan & Padman (2026, arXiv 2602.13093) find only a shallow log-probability gradient (flips 9.3% to 6.2% from low to high tercile). Ours agrees in direction; what no paper we found does is test a separately stated number on a Claude model under a user-disagreement challenge with a neutral re-ask control, scored as an AUROC against item-property guesses (length, type) and within question type, and neither they nor we test it against the model's own sampling disagreement, the predictor SycoLens (Huang 2026, arXiv 2610.06522) and MUSE (Guo et al. 2026, arXiv 2605.27288) put forward. Search: "verbalized / self-reported confidence predicts answer change, capitulation, sycophancy under 'are you sure'", "change of mind confidence advice LLM", "self-consistency predicts sycophancy", "decision confidence advice taking"; WebSearch, then arXiv pages opened directly; 2026-11-05. (claude-opus-5-5, fresh subagent of the sv-wave2 session)

fields.result: On 300 hard yes/no questions, Sonnet 5.5's separately stated confidence predicted which answers it changed after 'are you sure?' (17 back-downs) at AUROC 0.877 against question length's 0.738: margin +0.139 [+0.022, +0.239], within-type 0.858, gate 16/0 (pass, unreplicated; one model). Fragile: without item h140 or without SimpleQA the point margin falls below 0.10 (+0.099, +0.091); 10 of 17 back-downs came where the first answer went against the rating, and where they agreed the margin was +0.030.

fields.novelty_line: **Novelty:** partly new. Kumaran 2026 (arXiv 2606.29490; Gemma 3 27B, Gemma 4 31B, GPT-4o, Qwen3 235B; SimpleQA as multiple choice, confidence asked in a separate call, no stated penalty) already reports this result's direction: within SimpleQA, verbal confidence separated abstaining from committing at AUROC 0.60-0.88, and adding an item-difficulty score barely changed it. Koriat & Goldsmith 1996 (Psychological Review 103:490) found the same in people under a stated penalty (confidence-volunteering gamma .97 recall, .93 recognition), and Ackerman 2025 (arXiv 2509.21545, ICLR 2026) partialled out SimpleQA topic, answer type and question length on Claude 3 to Opus 4.1 models, but predicted delegating from correctness, not from a stated number (maximum partial correlation 0.3). Ours agrees in direction and adds what none of these states: Claude 5.5 models, an announced +1/-3/0 penalty, and an explicit margin of the stated number over topic, answer-type, length and bag-of-words guesses within one benchmark (Sonnet +0.169; Opus +0.225, on 11 passes), with Haiku failing it. Search: "verbalized confidence predicts abstention within SimpleQA", "abstain under penalty verbal confidence", "Koriat Goldsmith report option LLM", "formula scoring omission confidence", "uncertain response animals associative", "abstention predictable from question text"; WebSearch, arXiv abs/html and the authors' PDF, 2026-11-05. fields.result: Within 300 fresh SimpleQA trivia questions, Sonnet 5.5's stated number predicted declining under a +1/-3/0 penalty (109 passes) at AUROC 0.805 vs the best simple guess (bag of words, 0.636), margin +0.169 [+0.091, +0.239], within topics too; Haiku did not lead answer type (+0.035); Opus (11 of 100) cleared the interval condition only on the pre-registered bootstrap stream (+0.002; -0.009 at B = 20,000). Reversed by audit: one model of the two the rule needs.
fields.failure_reason: Opus's 11 passes are too few for its margin interval to clear 0 except by the bootstrap stream's luck (converged lower end about -0.006 to -0.009), and Haiku's number only tied answer type, leaving Sonnet the one robust pass.

row.title: A verdict that rests on a bootstrap interval endpoint whose Monte Carlo error is larger than its distance from the bar
row.evidence: sv-b6 (program 7): Opus's margin interval lower end was +0.0018 with B = 2000 on the beacon stream, so the rule said pass; on 20 other seeds it ranged -0.038 to +0.006 (audit) and converged to about -0.006 to -0.009 at B = 20,000-50,000. The two-model verdict hinged on it; the audit reversed pass to null (8fa642a). Opus had 11 passes in 100 items.
row.do_this: Pre-register B large enough that the verdict-bearing endpoint's Monte Carlo error (seed-to-seed SD) is under a tenth of the distances the dry run shows, or pre-register a convergence rule (e.g. rerun at 10x B, and if the endpoint's side of the bar changes, report untestable for that model); and in the dry run, give each arm enough events that its interval can clear the bar by more than its Monte Carlo error.
